procedures.anti_example: A broad request advances without one observable outcome.
finished: The observable outcome, owner, and task boundary are explicit.
good: One observable outcome names its owner and task boundary.

mentoring.lesson: Agentic delivery starts by converting a broad request into one observable outcome with a clear owner.
mentoring.recognition_heuristic: Use this procedure when the request names activity but not the externally visible result.
mentoring.why_gate_exists: Without an owned outcome, agents can produce substantial work that does not complete the user's goal.

rationale.summary: Is there one observable outcome with an owner and boundary?

procedures.anti_example: Work advances while authority or material unknowns remain implicit.
finished: Context, constraints, risks, authority, and unknowns are recorded.
good: The delivery boundary distinguishes known facts from unresolved questions.

mentoring.lesson: Good framing separates known facts, material unknowns, constraints, and decision authority before implementation.
mentoring.recognition_heuristic: Use this procedure when different answers to an unresolved question would change the solution or its owner.
mentoring.why_gate_exists: Implicit constraints and authority create rework, collisions, and decisions made by the wrong actor.

rationale.summary: Are context, constraints, risks, authority, and unknowns explicit?

procedures.anti_example: Implementation begins while observable behavior remains ambiguous.
finished: Behavior, interfaces, non-goals, and binary acceptance criteria are resolved.
good: The contract separates required behavior from explicit non-goals.

mentoring.lesson: A useful specification describes observable behavior, interfaces, non-goals, and binary acceptance evidence.
mentoring.recognition_heuristic: Use this procedure when two capable engineers could implement different behaviors from the same request.
mentoring.why_gate_exists: Implementation cannot be judged objectively while the expected behavior remains ambiguous.

rationale.summary: Are behavior, interfaces, non-goals, and binary acceptance criteria resolved?

procedures.anti_example: A task list omits ownership, proof, or a stop condition.
finished: Vertical slices, dependencies, ownership, proof, and stop rules are defined.
good: Each bounded slice names its dependency, owner, proof, and stop rule.

mentoring.lesson: A delivery plan should create small vertical slices that each produce usable evidence and have an explicit stop rule.
mentoring.recognition_heuristic: Use this procedure when work spans dependencies, owners, or proof surfaces that cannot safely change as one slice.
mentoring.why_gate_exists: A task list without dependencies, ownership, and proof hides the critical path and encourages unfinished parallel work.

rationale.summary: Are vertical slices, dependencies, ownership, proof, and stop rules defined?

procedures.anti_example: A broad implementation changes unrelated behavior to make tests pass.
finished: The smallest coherent implementation makes the accepted red case green.
good: The implementation is bounded to the behavior demonstrated by the red case.

mentoring.lesson: The implementation should be the smallest coherent change that turns an honest failing example into passing behavior.
mentoring.recognition_heuristic: Use this procedure after the expected behavior can fail observably and the change boundary is understood.
mentoring.why_gate_exists: Building before a trustworthy red case invites speculative code and makes success hard to distinguish from test weakness.

met.lesson: Both cases now bind this revision, so the remaining risk is scope: a change that passes its own two cases can still have moved behavior nobody asked it to move.
met.recognition_heuristic: Recognize this when the proof is green and the honest next question is what else the diff touched, not whether it works.
met.why_gate_exists: The gate opens on evidence, not on completeness. It cannot see work your change did outside the boundary the red case described.

partial.lesson: One half of a change's proof is not the change. A red case with no green one shows the behavior can fail; a green one with no red one shows a test that may never have been able to fail.
partial.recognition_heuristic: Recognize this when you can name the evidence you already have and have stopped naming the evidence you still owe.
partial.why_gate_exists: Partial proof is where a change feels finished and is not. The gate holds here because the missing half is the half that would have contradicted you.

rationale.summary: Does the smallest coherent implementation make an honest red case green?

procedures.anti_example: A passing test from another revision is treated as proof.
finished: Every required verification fact is accepted for the exact revision and environment.
good: Focused and integration evidence bind the exact revision and environment.

mentoring.lesson: Verification is evidence bound to the exact revision and environment, not a claim that testing happened.
mentoring.recognition_heuristic: Use this procedure when implementation is complete but its behavior has not been proven at all required boundaries.
mentoring.why_gate_exists: Passing evidence from another revision or environment can create a false green release decision.

met.lesson: Every required report is accepted for this exact revision and environment. That is a real result, and it is a claim about this revision only; it expires the moment the head moves.
met.recognition_heuristic: Recognize this when you are about to cite a passing run from before your last push as though it still applied.
met.why_gate_exists: Evidence is bound to a revision so a later commit cannot inherit an earlier commit's green. Rebasing does not carry proof with it.

partial.lesson: Focused and integration evidence answer different questions. One says the unit behaves; the other says it still behaves once something else is holding it. Neither substitutes for the other.
partial.recognition_heuristic: Recognize this when the report you have is the one that was easy to run, and the one you owe is the one that needs real dependencies.
partial.why_gate_exists: The boundary you did not test is the boundary that fails in production, because it is the one nobody was watching.

rationale.summary: Verification evidence is incomplete for the exact revision and environment.

procedures.anti_example: Approval from another revision is applied to the current change.
finished: Independent review covers the exact base, head, and accepted specification.
good: The reviewer records findings against the exact change and its contract.

mentoring.lesson: Independent review tests the exact change against its accepted contract and searches for risks the author missed.
mentoring.recognition_heuristic: Use this procedure when a candidate is green locally and needs a fresh perspective before publication.
mentoring.why_gate_exists: Author confidence and passing tests do not expose every contract gap, regression, or hidden assumption.

rationale.summary: Has an independent reviewer checked the exact base and head against the spec?

procedures.anti_example: A stale green check is treated as current merge-candidate evidence.
finished: All findings are resolved and required checks are current on the merge candidate.
good: The merge candidate binds resolved findings and required checks to one revision.

mentoring.lesson: A pull request becomes mergeable only when findings and required checks agree on the same immutable candidate.
mentoring.recognition_heuristic: Use this procedure when code is published but review or check evidence may be stale relative to the current head.
mentoring.why_gate_exists: A later push can invalidate earlier approval while leaving misleading green signals visible.

rationale.summary: Are findings resolved and required checks current on the merge candidate?

procedures.anti_example: A successful build is reported as proof that the revision is live.
finished: The intended revision is live, observed, and covered by a recovery path.
good: Deployment evidence binds the live observation and recovery path to one revision.

mentoring.lesson: Deployment is complete only when the intended revision is observed live and a recovery path is credible.
mentoring.recognition_heuristic: Use this procedure after release automation succeeds but before treating the user-facing outcome as delivered.
mentoring.why_gate_exists: A successful build or deploy command does not prove that users received the intended behavior.

rationale.summary: Is the intended revision live, observed, and recoverable?
